identification.summary: Iranian state-sponsored actor associated with an intelligence arm of the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC). It runs long-term espionage through targeted phishing and social engineering against dissidents, journalists, academics, think tanks, policymakers and government officials. One subgroup rapidly weaponizes newly public vulnerabilities against critical-infrastructure targets [S1]. It targeted a 2024 US presidential campaign [S2][S3].
identification.firstObserved: FireEye identified APT35 operations dating back to 2014 (imported record). Microsoft reports a subgroup moving from reconnaissance to direct targeting of US critical infrastructure from late 2021 to mid-2022 [S1].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Mint Sandstorm (formerly PHOSPHORUS). Microsoft maps CHARMING KITTEN, APT35, Newscaster and Parastoo to it [S5]. MITRE tracks it as Magic Hound (G0059) [S4]. Google/Mandiant's APT42 overlaps with part of this activity, and coverage of the 2024 election case uses 'Mint Sandstorm or APT42' interchangeably. This encyclopedia holds a separate APT42 record; vendor cluster boundaries differ.

attribution.sponsor: Islamic Republic of Iran: IRGC intelligence elements [S1]. The September 2024 indictment charged three individuals described as IRGC employees [S3].
attribution.confidence: Microsoft assesses the IRGC association, corroborated by Mandiant, Proofpoint and Secureworks; the US Treasury sanctioned elements of the group in 2022 citing IRGC sponsorship [S1]. Formal US attribution through the 2024 indictment of three named IRGC employees for the campaign hack [S3].
attribution.basis: Microsoft telemetry and vendor corroboration [S1]; DOJ indictment [S3]; Treasury sanctions (2022), as cited by Microsoft [S1].

objectives: Intelligence collection in support of IRGC priorities: monitoring dissidents and activists, collecting on foreign policy, defense and nuclear-related experts, and gaining access to critical infrastructure that could support retaliation [S1]. In 2024 it ran a hack-and-leak operation against a US presidential campaign, attempting to pass stolen material to people it believed were tied to the opposing campaign [S3].

sectors: Government and policy (current and former officials)
Critical infrastructure: seaports, energy, transit, a major US utility and gas entity (subgroup)
targeting.notes: Sector targeting from Microsoft [S1] and the 2024 indictment [S3]. Phishing against Israeli, North American and European think tanks and universities per Microsoft [S1].

capabilities.summary: Social engineering is the core tradecraft: tailored spear-phishing, impersonation and credential harvesting, including multi-week rapport building before delivery [S1][S3]. A subgroup weaponizes public proofs of concept within days: Zoho ManageEngine CVE-2022-47966 (exploited the day the PoC appeared), IBM Aspera Faspex CVE-2022-47986 (within five days) and Log4Shell [S1]. Custom tooling includes Drokbk and Soldier (.NET implants) and CharmPower (modular PowerShell backdoor delivered through template injection) [S1].

campaigns.name: US presidential campaign hack-and-leak
campaigns.summary: Compromise of accounts tied to a presidential campaign, then attempts to leak stolen material. Microsoft reported spear-phishing of a high-ranking campaign official in June 2024. DOJ unsealed charges against three IRGC employees on 27 Sep 2024.

diamond.adversary: IRGC intelligence elements; three named IRGC employees charged in 2024 [S1][S3].
diamond.capability: Spear-phishing and persona operations; credential harvesting; rapid n-day exploitation; Drokbk, Soldier, CharmPower [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: Lookalike domains and fake personas for phishing; actor-controlled C2 for .NET and PowerShell implants. Reporting links the 2024 indictees to the Iranian ISP Respina Networks (secondary coverage) [S3].
diamond.victim: Dissidents, journalists, academics, think tanks, policymakers, a US presidential campaign, and US critical infrastructure (subgroup) [S1][S3].
diamond.socioPolitical: Regime security and foreign-policy intelligence; influence on US politics through hack-and-leak; retaliatory positioning against adversary infrastructure [S1][S3].
diamond.technology: Exploits human trust (email and social media) and slow patching of internet-facing enterprise applications [S1].

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: The OE includes the personal accounts and devices of staff, policy advisers and family members, because this actor works through people more than networks. STEP 2: In a US–Iran crisis, expect collection against planners, think tanks and media plus opportunistic access to US port, energy and transit infrastructure. STEP 3: The template is persona-driven rapport building, then credential phishing or a malicious template, then a PowerShell or .NET implant. In parallel, a separate team exploits newly published CVEs within days. STEP 4: MLCOA is intensified phishing of government, military and policy personnel to inform IRGC decision-making. MDCOA is hack-and-leak or opportunistic infrastructure disruption timed to political events or military action. Candidate indicators: new lookalike domains for US government or think-tank brands, phishing that references real conferences or interviews, and exploitation within days of a public PoC [S1][S3].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Personnel-centric defense: phishing-resistant MFA and reporting channels for personal accounts of key staff are C2 protection measures. (2) Patch tempo as an operational metric: the subgroup's days-to-exploit window means JCC2 situational awareness should track exposure time on internet-facing systems, not just patch compliance. (3) Information environment: hack-and-leak threats require coordination with public affairs and counterintelligence before material surfaces. (4) Authorities: election and campaign infrastructure defense is led by the FBI and CISA, so DoD's role is limited to its own personnel and networks.

provenance.importedSummary: FireEye has identified APT35 operations dating back to 2014. APT35, also known as the Newscaster Team, is a threat group sponsored by the Iranian government that conducts long term, resource-intensive operations to collect strategic intelligence. APT35 typically targets U.S. and the Middle Eastern military, diplomatic and government personnel, organizations in the media, energy and defense industrial base (DIB), and engineering, business services and telecommunications sectors.
